sections.h2: Where Macon County deeds are filed
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded at the Macon County Register of Deeds in Franklin. County government works from 5 West Main Street, Franklin, NC 28734, and the switchboard at (828) 349-2000 can connect you to the office.

Call ahead for the recording hours and the same-day cutoff before you plan a closing around them.

The register is elected by county voters for a two-year term under G.S. 161-1. Recording follows statewide rules, so a Macon County deed uses the same format, fee and tax rules as a deed filed in any other North Carolina county.

Fees come from G.S. 161-10, and the excise tax comes from G.S. 105-228.30. The register collects both before a deed is recorded.

  • Ordinary instruments: a $26 base for up to 15 pages, with $4 for each page past that.
  • Mortgages and deeds of trust: a $64 base for up to 35 pages, again $4 for each extra page.
  • Satisfactions and cancellations of mortgages and deeds of trust: no fee.
  • A second instrument in the same document: $10.
  • Excise tax: $1 per $500 of value, rounded up for any partial block.

The seller is the transferor and owes the excise tax. The county keeps half for its general fund, and the rest goes to state revenue officials monthly, net of refunds and the county's allowance. Closing attorneys in Franklin normally deduct the tax from the seller's proceeds and deliver it with the deed.

Filing sets priority. G.S. 47-18 withholds protection from deeds, sale contracts, options and leases over three years until they are registered where the land lies, and whoever registers first comes first.

A parcel that has changed hands through several families can carry old rights of way or boundary agreements. Your closing attorney should search the Macon County index under every prior owner. Pick up the parcel map from Land Records as well, so the new deed's legal description lines up with the tax parcel.

Filing a deed does not itself clear the tax bill. The county assesses property as of January 1, so ask the tax office who is billed for the current year and plan the proration with your closing attorney.

The Land Records office, also called the Mapping Office, is on the main level of the Macon County Courthouse on the Square in downtown Franklin. It is the place to get property cards, parcel maps and county maps, and it has public terminals for document searches, property searches, collection information and assessment data.

The tax office website links an address change form, property tax forms and a land records search, so many owners can pull a map or a parcel record before they visit. A seller preparing a listing can print the parcel map to check the lot lines against the deed.

The Tax Department itself sits in the annex at 5 West Main Street. It posts a separate tax scroll for Highlands next to the county scroll.

The county tax calendar drives most of what follows a sale. The Macon County Tax Department lists these dates.

Macon County tax calendar
DateWhat happens
January 1Date of assessment; personal property ownership and place of taxation are set as of this date
January 1 to 31Listing period for personal property, except tagged motor vehicles, and for exemption and exclusion filing
January 5Last day to pay property taxes without interest
January 6Interest begins
AprilReview board hears appeals
April 15Last date to file listings with a prior approved extension
AugustCurrent-year tax bills processed and mailed

Appeals must be received or postmarked by the day the review board adjourns each April. A 2027 reappraisal is coming, and the tax office runs an online appeal portal, so use it after new values are mailed.

sections.h2: Paying a bill and avoiding scams
sections.html:
Bill payment runs on a newer platform, so owners need to register their accounts again and re-enroll in paperless billing. The portal is open around the clock and includes AutoPay, text alerts with pay-by-text, and an automated pay-by-phone line. Collections answers at (828) 349-2142.

The tax office also warns about lookalike government scams. The Macon County Tax Office does not contact taxpayers asking to come to their homes to collect a debt. If a caller does, share no personal information and hang up at once. Sellers who owe back taxes are a likely target, so route any demand through the official office and your closing attorney.

Businesses must list business personal property each January under G.S. 105-308, which covers furniture, fixtures, machinery and similar equipment. A rental owner who keeps furnishings in an income-producing unit should ask the Personal Property desk at (828) 349-2144 whether those items need listing.

Macon County includes Franklin, Highlands and Nantahala, and has 39,232 residents, up 6.0 percent from 2020. It has 27,700 housing units but only 18,406 households, and owners occupy 77.6 percent of homes. The typical owner-occupied home is worth $251,900. A buyer planning a second home or a rental will want to see the recorded deed and any restrictions on file with the register.

Call the clerk of superior court before the register of deeds. The Estates and Special Proceedings line is (828) 349-7204, and that office can explain whether a small estate affidavit fits or whether the estate needs a personal representative.

For intestate estates, G.S. 28A-25-1 permits an affidavit filed with the clerk in the county of domicile when personal property less liens does not exceed $20,000, any time after 30 days from death. A surviving spouse who is the only heir may reach a limit up to $30,000 after the spousal allowance. The affidavit lists each tract of land the person owned.

When someone has authority to sign, the deed then goes to the Register of Deeds. Bring the certified death record if the register or the title company asks for it.

sections.h2: Getting a Macon County deed recorded, step by step
sections.html:
1. Confirm who must sign, including spouses and any heirs, and get the deed notarized.
  2. Ask the tax office who is billed for the current year and settle the proration with your closing attorney.
  3. Match the legal description to the parcel map from Land Records.
  4. Pay the page fee and the excise tax, normally deducted from the seller's proceeds by the closing attorney.
  5. Have a lender's satisfaction recorded for any old mortgage or deed of trust, which carries no fee.
  6. Keep the recorded copy with your closing papers.

A cash sale follows the same steps. What it skips is the lender's appraisal and underwriting, so liens, back taxes and estate paperwork are the items to line up first.

faqs.q: Where is the Macon County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: The office is part of Macon County government in Franklin, whose main address is 5 West Main Street, Franklin, NC 28734. Call (828) 349-2000 and ask for the Register of Deeds to confirm hours.

faqs.q: What do Macon County deed filings cost?
faqs.a: An ordinary instrument starts at $26 for up to 15 pages, with $4 per page after that, and the excise tax adds $1 per $500 of value. The office collects both before it records the deed.

faqs.q: Does Macon County have a separate tax scroll for Highlands?
faqs.a: Yes. The Macon County Tax Department posts a separate tax scroll for Highlands next to the main county scroll. Ask the tax office which scroll applies to your parcel.

faqs.q: When do Macon County property taxes become late?
faqs.a: January 5 is the last day to pay clear of interest, which starts January 6. Current-year bills are processed and mailed in August.

faqs.q: Where can I get a parcel map in Macon County?
faqs.a: Visit the Land Records office in the Macon County Courthouse on the Square in Franklin, or use the land records search linked from the tax office page. Property cards, parcel maps and county maps are available there.
